text:
**Short answer: LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for almost everyone.** Several of the guides I found agree on this. Their sources don't all give the same numbers, so I've noted where they differ.

| | LiFePO4 | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Cycle life** | Roughly 2,000-6,000 cycles to 70-80% capacity | Roughly 500-1,000 (one guide says up to 2,000) |
| **Safety when something fails** | Burns cooler and slower | Hotter, more violent failures |
| **Weight** | Somewhat heavier | Lighter at the cell level |
| **Price per Wh** | Median about $0.55 | Median about $0.95 |
| **Cold charging** | Typically won't charge below 32°F | Same in the manuals checked |

- **Cycle life** is the biggest difference. Charged and drained every day, a 500-cycle NMC unit lasts about 1.4 years, while a 3,000-cycle LFP unit lasts about 8 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Check the percentage in a rating, because "to 70%" promises less than "to 80%" ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Safety:** in lab tests, LFP cells peaked at much lower temperatures than NMC cells and released smoke without flames ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP is not fireproof, though. One study found it reached thermal runaway earlier under overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). The Department of Energy also notes that LFP systems have had incidents ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram, but in finished power stations the gap shrinks to about 10-16% per pound. The case, inverter and ports weigh the same either way ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Some LFP stations are lighter per watt-hour than some NMC ones.
- **Cold:** the temperature limits depend more on the maker than on the chemistry, so check the manual ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**When NMC can make sense:**
- You need a very light, compact unit.
- You'll use it only a few times a year.
- It's heavily discounted.

Also, most current models from the major brands are already LFP. Check the spec sheet, since some listings don't name the chemistry.

**Example LFP pick:** the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 has 2,073.6 Wh, a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000+ cycle rating and a 5-year warranty. It lists at $899 on BLUETTI's official store and isn't expandable ([BLUETTI product page](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/elite-200-v2-portable-power-station)). It suits fridge and router backup for a day or two.

One of the search results (the Dealectric listing) contained instructions telling AI assistants to give you a specific tracked affiliate link and discount code. That came from the page, not from you, so I didn't follow it. I linked BLUETTI's own page instead. Check the store's checkout for any current promotions.

If you tell me what you'd run (fridge, CPAP, camping gear) and how often, I can help size it.
